newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe, S.Africa reach outline farm trade deal.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe, S.Africa reach outline farm trade deal.

text.p: Zimbabwe and South Africa announced on Thursday that they had reached a broad agreement on trade in agricultural products, but said tobacco and citrus still required further discussion.

Zimbabwe Industry and Commerce Minister Nathan Shamuyarira and South African Trade and Industry Minister Alec Erwin told a news conference the agreement was reached at talks they held on the sidelines of a Southern African Economic Summit in Harare.
They said the farm trade deal was a big step in the two countries' drive to seal a comprehensive trade pact soon, an issue that has caused tension between them over the last three years.
"We have made further progress. Today, we focused on agricultural and animal products, and I am pleased to announce that we have reached a broad agreement on a number of items," Shamuyarira said.
"The only sticking points are citrus and tobacco...and we shall be discussing these further after consulting industry," he said.
Erwin said he was keen to ensure that Zimbabwe citrus, which in the past had been been attacked by a fungal disease, would not carry the disease into South Africa.
He said South Africa also wanted to consult its industry on whether Zimbabwean tobacco should enjoy preferential entry into the country.
"We hope this can be wrapped up within a month," Shamuyarira said.

Negotiations to update an expired 1964 trade agreement have gone on since 1992. Zimbabwean business and government leaders have consistently accused South Africa of dragging its feet in concluding the agreement, despite South Africa's vehement denials.

South Africa is Zimbabwe's largest trading partner in Africa but the trade is heavily weighted in South Africa's favour. In 1995, trade between the two nations totalled Z$10 billion (U.S.$885 million).
